meta.title: Khmer A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Khmer is the language of Cambodia. Both study directions in one deck: Khmer → English (see the Khmer, recall the meaning) and English → Khmer (see an English meaning, recall the Khmer). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Khmer, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 302 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, jobs, work and study, clothes, cooking and more food, the furniture of a home, the town and its buildings, travel and directions, nature and animals, the rainy and the dry season, health and the body, feelings and character, free time, sport and festivals, telling what happened and when, comparing and giving an opinion, phones and the internet, measures, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing and doing — and the other 448 are the commonest remaining words of Khmer, counted in the articles of the Khmer Wikipedia. The first day's greetings come first and the rest are dealt by that count, so the words you meet most often come early; an encyclopaedia's commonest words lean towards the written language. Every headword is printed in Khmer script with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it, a phonetic spelling that shows the vowel each letter's series gives it (ក with ា is kaa, គ with ា is kiə) — the Khmer Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the two series. There are no forms to learn: Khmer words never change shape. Real example sentences come with 278 of the 750 words, three apiece for 86 of them — the sources hold few Khmer sentences — with the word picked out in colour. There is no speaker button, since few devices have a Khmer voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation and some example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0), via the kaikki.org extraction and the entries' own pages. Frequency: the Khmer Wikipedia, the dump of 1 November 2026 (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
